name: System writing tools (Writing Tools, ML Kit Summarization and Rewriting)
plain: Offers rewrite, proofread and summarise inside any text field.
meaning: Writing Tools appear automatically in standard text views on iOS. On Android, apps call task APIs for summarize, proofread, rewrite and describe image.

android.permission: None; ML Kit GenAI Summarization, Proofreading, Rewriting, Image Description APIs
android.note: Android has no automatic system wide writing tools in all text fields; apps integrate APIs.

ios.permission: None; UITextView supports by default; opt out via writingToolsBehavior
ios.prompt_ui: Writing Tools menu in selection; Apple Intelligence required
ios.note: Handled in system; may use Private Cloud Compute for longer text.

limits.headline: Can offer rewrite, proofread and summarize inside text boxes, if Apple Intelligence is on
limits.user_action: You select text and tap Writing Tools, or an app's own rewrite button
can: Rewrite, proofread or summarize text you select on iPhone
Use Apple's private cloud for longer text, when needed
Call on Android's own tools through the app, like Summarization and Rewriting
cannot: Work on every iPhone; Apple Intelligence is needed
Work in all text fields on Android automatically; apps must add support
Change your text unless you tap to accept the suggestion
limits.differs: iPhone has a system wide Writing Tools menu. Android has no automatic system tools in every text field.

story.what_it_is: Built in rewrite, proofread and summarize tools that appear in text fields.

marketing.name: Writing Tools
marketing.pitch: Apple pitches Writing Tools as a way to rewrite, proofread and summarize text anywhere you write.

marketing.name: ML Kit GenAI Summarization
marketing.pitch: Google offers on device summarization for apps through ML Kit.

story.for_you: You select text and a menu offers Rewrite, Proofread or Summarize. On iPhone it works in most apps automatically. On Android it depends on the app.
story.for_makers: Makers get smart text help with little work on iOS, and must add the API on Android. Long text may go to Apple's private cloud, so privacy rules matter.

use_cases.example: You fix a typo ridden message before sending it.
You summarize a long email thread in one tap.
You rewrite a post to sound friendlier.
A manager makes a message more professional.
A writing app offers a shorter version.
A reader gets a short summary of a hard page.

risks: Longer text may leave the phone
story.android_note: No automatic system wide tools. Apps add ML Kit task APIs.
story.ios_note: Needs Apple Intelligence. It may use Private Cloud Compute for longer text.

abuse: Leaking text to cloud for large input on iOS
